A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ILK is an Mn2+-dependent protein kinase that regulates the phosphorylation of the GSK-3β protein kinase and the LC20 regulatory subunit of nonmuscle myosin.
ILK is an active, Mn2+-dependent kinase with a preference for peptide substrates with a proline at P-1 and P-3 positions.
ILK is the only known protein kinase that can utilize either Mg2+ or Mn2+ for its enzymatic activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ILK is not only an active protein kinase, but also that it is a Mn2+-dependent kinase.
ILK is not only capable of phosphorylating a variety of peptide and protein substrates, but it can do so at physiological concentrations of ATP and in the absence of exogenous ATP.
ILK can be added to the list of protein kinases that are regulated by divalent metal ions.
